sections.title: 1. Filesystem, paths and commands
sections.md:
- **Inode**: stores a file's metadata (type, owner, size, times, where the data is) but **not its name**.
- **Directory**: a file whose contents map **filenames to inode numbers**. A regular file is an ordinary data file; directories are not regular files.
- **Hard link**: a directory entry (name → inode). Every file has at least one. The number after the permissions in `ls -l` is the hard-link count.
- Root directory: `/`. **Absolute** path starts at `/` (`/home/user1/notes`); **relative** path starts at the current working directory (`notes`, `../user2`).

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.` | current directory |
| `..` | parent directory |
| `~` | your home directory (`~user2` = user2's home) |
| `cd` | (no argument) go home |
| `cd -` | go back to the previous directory (prints it) |
| `pwd` | print the absolute path of the working directory |

**Command form**: `command -options arguments`. Options combine: `ls -s -h` = `ls -sh`. Long form: `--all`.

| `ls` option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-a` | all files, including hidden (`.name`) and `.` `..` |
| `-A` | like `-a` but not `.` and `..` |
| `-d` | list a directory itself, not its contents |
| `-l` | long listing |
| `-1` | one name per line |
| `-r` | reverse order |
| `-t` | sort by modification time (newest first) |
| `-S` | sort by size (largest first) |
| `-s` / `-h` | size in blocks / human readable |
| `-F` | add a symbol showing the file type |

Kinds of commands: built-in (`cd`, `pwd`), executable program (`ls`), alias, shell function. `type cmd` says which; `which cmd` gives the program's path. Help: `man ls`, `ls --help`, `help cd` (built-ins).

**Lists of commands**: `a; b` runs both in order. `a && b` runs `b` only if `a` succeeds (exit status 0). `a || b` runs `b` only if `a` fails. `cmd &` runs in the background.

sections.title: 2. Filename expansion (globs)
sections.md:
An **unquoted** word containing `*`, `?` or `[` is replaced by the **alphabetically sorted** list of matching filenames. Globs do not match hidden files (leading `.`) unless the pattern starts with `.`.

| Wildcard | Matches |
|---|---|
| `*` | any string, including the empty string |
| `?` | exactly one character |
| `[abc]` | one character from the set |
| `[a-z]` `[0-9]` | one character in the range |
| `[!abc]` | one character **not** in the set |
| `[[:upper:]]` | one character in a POSIX class |

POSIX classes (only inside `[ ]`): `[:alpha:]` `[:digit:]` `[:alnum:]` `[:upper:]` `[:lower:]` `[:space:]` `[:blank:]` `[:punct:]`.

```bash
ls *.txt                 # names ending in .txt
ls ???                   # names exactly 3 characters long
ls *.[pP][dD][fF]        # .pdf in any mix of case
ls */A1answers.txt       # that file in every subdirectory
ls -d */                 # just the subdirectories
cp * ../backup           # every (non-hidden) file here
```

If nothing matches, the pattern is left **as is** (e.g. `*.pdf` stays the literal string `*.pdf`). In a `for` loop guard with `[[ -e $f ]] || continue`.

sections.title: 3. Quoting
sections.md:
| Form | Effect |
|---|---|
| `\c` | escape: the next character is literal (`file\ name`) |
| `'...'` | everything literal; no expansions at all; cannot contain `'` |
| `"..."` | literal **except** `$` (parameter, `$( )`, `$(( ))`), backquote and `\` |

Double quotes stop **word splitting**, **filename expansion**, tilde and brace expansion, but still allow `$var`, `$(cmd)`, `$((expr))`.

```bash
x="a   b"
echo $x          # a b        (split into 2 words, joined by one space)
echo "$x"        # a   b
echo '$x'        # $x
echo "*"         # *          (no globbing)
```

**Always write `"$var"`, `"$1"`, `"$@"`, `"${arr[@]}"`** in scripts: a filename with a space otherwise becomes several arguments. Inside `[[ ]]` the left side does not need quotes (no word splitting there), but quote the right side of `==`/`!=` to compare literally.

sections.title: 4. Files: create, move, copy, remove, link
sections.md:
Any character except `/` and the null character can be in a filename. Names are case sensitive; a leading `.` means hidden. Avoid spaces and a leading `-`.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `touch f1 f2` | create empty files (or update the timestamp) |
| `mkdir d1 d2` | create directories |
| `mkdir -p a/b/c` | create missing parents too; no error if it exists |
| `mv old new` | rename (overwrites `new` if it exists) |
| `mv f1 f2 dir` | move files into an existing directory |
| `cp src dst` | copy a file |
| `cp f1 f2 dir` | copy several files into a directory |
| `cp -r dir1 dir2` | copy a directory and its contents |
| `rm f1 f2` | remove files (permanent!) |
| `rm -r dir` | remove a directory and everything inside |
| `rmdir dir` | remove an **empty** directory |
| `ln target name` | hard link: a second name for the same inode |
| `ln -s target name` | symbolic link: a file that points to a name |
| `cat f` | print a file's contents |

`-i` (`mv -i`, `rm -i`, `cp -i`) asks before overwriting/removing. Removing one hard link only decreases the link count; the data is gone when the count reaches 0. A symbolic link breaks (dangles) if its target is renamed or removed.

sections.title: 5. Permissions
sections.md:
`ls -l` shows: type+permissions, hard links, owner, group, size, time, name.

`-rwxr-x---` = type `-` (regular file; `d` directory, `l` symbolic link) then **user** `rwx`, **group** `r-x`, **other** `---`.

| | Regular file | Directory |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | read contents | list names (with `x`) |
| `w` | change contents | create/delete/rename files in it (with `x`) |
| `x` | run as a program | enter it (`cd`) |

**Octal**: r=4, w=2, x=1, one digit each for user, group, other.

| Octal | Meaning | Octal | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | `rwx` | 3 | `-wx` |
| 6 | `rw-` | 2 | `-w-` |
| 5 | `r-x` | 1 | `--x` |
| 4 | `r--` | 0 | `---` |

```bash
chmod 750 hello.sh        # rwxr-x---
chmod 644 notes.txt       # rw-r--r--
chmod 700 .trash          # rwx------
```

**Symbolic**: who `u g o a` + operator `+` add, `-` remove, `=` set exactly + perms `r w x`. Separate with commas, no spaces.

```bash
chmod u+x script.sh       # add execute for the owner
chmod go-w *.txt          # remove write for group and other
chmod u=rw,go=r f         # rw-r--r--
chmod u=rwx,go= dir       # rwx------  (empty = none)
stat -c %a f              # prints the octal permissions, e.g. 644
```

sections.title: 6. Streams, redirection, pipes and tee
sections.md:
File descriptors: **0** standard input, **1** standard output, **2** standard error.

| Syntax | Effect |
|---|---|
| `cmd > f` | stdout to `f` (create/overwrite); same as `1>` |
| `cmd >> f` | append stdout to `f` |
| `cmd 2> f` | stderr to `f` |
| `cmd > out 2> err` | stdout and stderr to separate files |
| `cmd > f 2>&1` | both to `f` (order matters: left to right) |
| `cmd 2> /dev/null` | throw error messages away |
| `echo "msg" >&2` | print a message **to standard error** |
| `cmd < f` | stdin from file `f` |

**Pipe** `a | b` sends the stdout of `a` to the stdin of `b`. **`tee f`** copies its input to the file `f` and to stdout, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| `sort` | sort lines (`-n` numeric, `-r` reverse) |
| `uniq` | remove **adjacent** duplicate lines (`-d` only duplicates); sort first |
| `wc -l` | count lines |
| `cut -d, -f2` | field 2 using `,` as the delimiter (default delimiter is tab) |
| `head -n 3` | first 3 lines |
| `grep -E 're' f` | lines matching an extended regex (`-n` line numbers, `-i` ignore case) |

```bash
cut -f3 classlist | sort | tee snum | head -n 3
ls /bin /usr/bin | sort | uniq -d | wc -l
```

sections.title: 7. tr: translate, delete, squeeze characters
sections.md:
`tr` reads **standard input only** and writes standard output. To use it on a variable, pipe the value in.

```bash
y=$(printf %s "$x" | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z')     # to uppercase
echo "$x" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'   # same with POSIX classes
echo "$x" | tr '.' '/'                   # every . becomes /
echo "$x" | tr -d '0-9'                  # delete all digits
echo "$x" | tr -s ' '                    # squeeze runs of spaces into one
echo "$x" | tr '[:digit:]' '[X*]'        # every digit becomes X
```

- Character *i* of `seq1` is replaced by character *i* of `seq2`; other characters pass through.
- If `seq2` is shorter, GNU `tr` repeats its last character (`[c*]` is the portable way).
- Duplicated characters in `seq1` give undefined results.

sections.title: 8. Expansions
sections.md:
Order the shell performs them: **1** brace, **2** tilde, **3** parameter, **4** command substitution and **5** arithmetic (left to right), **6** word splitting, **7** filename expansion.

| Expansion | Example | Result |
|---|---|---|
| brace list | `echo f{a,b,c}.txt` | `fa.txt fb.txt fc.txt` |
| brace sequence | `echo {1..5}` | `1 2 3 4 5` |
| with step | `echo {10..20..5}` | `10 15 20` |
| zero padded | `echo {08..10}` | `08 09 10` |
| letters | `echo {a..e}` | `a b c d e` |
| tilde | `echo ~` | `/home/user1` |
| parameter | `echo "$x"` / `"${x}"` | value of `x` |
| command substitution | `d=$(pwd)` | output of the command (trailing newlines removed) |
| arithmetic | `echo $(( 2 * 5 ))` | `10` |

- `mkdir {2023..2024}-{01..12}` makes 24 directories.
- **Word splitting** happens on unquoted results, at the characters in `IFS` (default space, tab, newline). Several separators in a row count as one.
- Change `IFS` temporarily to split on something else: `IFS=","` then `for f in $str`, then restore it.
- In an **assignment** `v=...` there is **no** brace expansion, **no** filename expansion and no word splitting; tilde, parameter, command and arithmetic expansion do happen. `x=*.txt` stores the literal `*.txt`.

sections.title: 9. Scripts, variables and command line arguments
sections.md:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# a comment (from # to end of line; a quoted # is not a comment)
echo "Hello, $1!"
```

Run it: `chmod u+x hello.sh` then `./hello.sh Sam` (or `bash hello.sh Sam` without execute permission).

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `$#` | number of command line arguments |
| `$0` | pathname used to run the script |
| `$1` ... `$9`, `${10}` | the arguments (braces needed from 10 on) |
| `"$@"` | all arguments, each as a separate word (use this to loop) |
| `"$*"` | all arguments as one string |
| `$?` | exit status of the last command (0 = success, 1-255 = failure) |

- `exit n` ends the script with status *n*; without it the status is that of the last command.
- `shift` drops `$1` and moves `$2` to `$1` and so on (`$#` decreases).
- **Assignment**: `name=value` with **no spaces** around `=`. Use the value with `$name` or `${name}`.
- Values are strings; unset variables expand to the empty string (no error).
- Concatenate by writing values next to each other: `str3=$str1$str2`, `out="${in}_.bak"` (braces needed because `$in_` would be the variable `in_`).
- Command output into a variable: `perm=$(stat -c %a "$src")`.
- Usage check pattern:

```bash
if (( $# != 1 )); then
    echo "Usage: script.sh name" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

sections.title: 10. Strings: parameter expansion
sections.md:
Example values: `s=abcdefghij`, `f=dir/file.txt.zip`.

| Expansion | Meaning | Example → result |
|---|---|---|
| `${#s}` | length | `10` |
| `${s:2}` | from index 2 to the end | `cdefghij` |
| `${s:3:4}` | 4 characters from index 3 | `defg` |
| `${s: -3}` | last 3 (space before `-`) | `hij` |
| `${s:1:-2}` | from 1 up to (not incl.) 2nd last | `bcdefgh` |
| `${f#*.}` | remove **shortest** leading match | `txt.zip` |
| `${f##*.}` | remove **longest** leading match | `zip` (extension) |
| `${f##*/}` | ... up to the last `/` | `file.txt.zip` (filename) |
| `${f%.*}` | remove **shortest** trailing match | `dir/file.txt` |
| `${f%%.*}` | remove **longest** trailing match | `dir/file` |
| `${f%/*}` | ... from the last `/` | `dir` (directory) |
| `${s/b/X}` | replace first match | `aXcdefghij` |
| `${s//[aeiou]/}` | replace all matches (here: delete vowels) | `bcdfghj` |
| `${s^}` / `${s^^}` | uppercase first / all characters | `Abcdefghij` / `ABCDEFGHIJ` |
| `${s,}` / `${s,,}` | lowercase first / all | |

Memory aid: `#` is on the left of `$` on the keyboard (removes from the **front**), `%` is on the right (removes from the **back**). Doubling the symbol makes the match **longest**. The variable itself is not changed.

Character at index *i*: `${s:i:1}`. Loop over characters: `for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ ))`.

| Expansion | `str` unset | `str` empty | `str` set |
|---|---|---|---|
| `${str:-word}` | `word` | `word` | `$str` |
| `${str:=word}` | `word`, assigns it | `word`, assigns it | `$str` |
| `${str:+word}` | nothing | nothing | `word` |
| `${str:?word}` | error, exit | error, exit | `$str` |

Without the `:` (e.g. `${str-word}`) only *unset* is tested, not empty.

sections.title: 11. Arithmetic
sections.md:
Integers only (no floating point). Operators as in Java/C: `+ - * / %`, `**` (power), `++ --`, `+= -= *= /=`, comparisons `< <= > >= == !=`, logic `&& || !`. Division truncates: `$(( 7 / 2 ))` is `3`.

| Form | Use |
|---|---|
| `(( expr ))` | command: do arithmetic or test; `$` optional on variable names |
| `$(( expr ))` | expansion: substitutes the value |

```bash
(( x = 1 + 2 ))           # x is 3
(( count++ ))
n=$(( ${#s} / 2 ))
echo "$(( 2 ** 10 ))"     # 1024
if (( val % 2 == 0 )); then echo even; fi
```

- **Exit status of `(( ))`**: 0 (true) if the value is **non-zero**, 1 (false) if the value is **0**. So `(( 5 - 5 ))` has status 1.
- Non-numeric, empty or unset variables count as 0 inside `(( ))`.
- `$RANDOM`: a random integer 0 to 32767; `$(( RANDOM % n ))` gives 0 to n-1.

sections.title: 12. Regular expressions
sections.md:
Bash uses POSIX **extended** regexes with `=~` inside `[[ ]]`. The match succeeds if the pattern matches **any part** of the string, so anchor with `^...$` to match the whole string. **Do not quote the regex** (quoted parts are matched literally); storing it in a variable `re='...'` then `[[ $s =~ $re ]]` is safe.

| Metacharacter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `^` / `$` | start / end of the string (line) |
| `.` | any single character |
| `[abc]` `[a-z]` `[[:digit:]]` | one character from the set |
| `[^abc]` | one character **not** in the set |
| `( )` | subexpression (group) |
| `*` | preceding atom **0 or more** times |
| `+` | preceding atom **1 or more** times |
| `?` | preceding atom **0 or 1** time |
| `{m,n}` `{m}` `{m,}` | between m and n / exactly m / at least m times |

- **Choice** `a|b` matches either side: `^(cat|dog)$` matches `cat` or `dog`.
- An **atom** is one character, a bracket expression or a subexpression.
- Metacharacters are literal inside `[ ]`: `^a[.]c$` matches `a.c`.
- `^(19|20)[0-9][0-9]$` matches the years 1900 to 2099.

| Regex | Matches |
|---|---|
| `^[0-9]+$` | unsigned integer |
| `^[-+]?[0-9]+$` | signed or unsigned integer |
| `^[a-z]+$` | one or more lowercase letters only |
| `^[A-Z]{4}[0-9]{3}$` | `CISC220` |
| `[[:space:]]` | contains whitespace |

```bash
if [[ $pw =~ [[:digit:]] ]]; then echo "has a digit"; fi
grep -E '^zip' file      # grep -E uses the same syntax on each line
```

Do not confuse with globs: in a regex `*` means "repeat the previous atom", in a glob `*` means "any string".

sections.title: 13. Conditions: [[ ]], if and logical operators
sections.md:
```bash
if [[ -f $file ]]; then
    echo "regular file"
elif [[ -d $file ]]; then
    echo "directory"
else
    echo "something else" >&2
fi
```

Spaces are required inside `[[ ` and ` ]]`. `if` runs any command and tests its **exit status** (0 = true): `if cd "$dir" 2> /dev/null; then ...`. One line: `if [[ ! -r $f ]]; then echo "not readable"; fi`.

| File test | True if |
|---|---|
| `-e f` | exists (any kind) |
| `-f f` | is a regular file |
| `-d f` | is a directory |
| `-r f` / `-w f` / `-x f` | readable / writable / executable |
| `-s f` | exists and size > 0 |
| `f1 -nt f2` / `-ot` | newer / older than |

| String test | True if |
|---|---|
| `-z $s` | empty |
| `-n $s` or just `$s` | not empty |
| `$a == $b` (or `=`) | equal; **unquoted** right side is a glob pattern (`$s == a*`) |
| `$a != $b` | not equal |
| `$a < $b` / `$a > $b` | before / after in dictionary order (strings, not numbers!) |
| `$s =~ regex` | regex match |
| `-v name` | variable `name` is set (no `$`) |

| Integer test (in `[[ ]]`) | Same with `(( ))` |
|---|---|
| `-eq` `-ne` | `==` `!=` |
| `-lt` `-le` | `<` `<=` |
| `-gt` `-ge` | `>` `>=` |

**Combine** (highest precedence first): `( expr )`, `! expr`, `expr1 && expr2`, `expr1 || expr2`. Examples: `[[ -f $f && -r $f ]]`, `(( yr % 400 == 0 || (yr % 4 == 0 && yr % 100 != 0) ))`.

Pitfall: `[[ 100 < 2 ]]` is **true** (string comparison). Use `(( 100 < 2 ))` or `-lt` for numbers.

sections.title: 14. Loops
sections.md:
```bash
for arg in "$@"; do              # each command line argument
    echo "$arg"
done

for f in *.txt; do               # each matching file
    [[ -e $f ]] || continue      # skip if the glob matched nothing
    mv "$f" "${f%.txt}.md"
done

for i in {1..5}; do echo "$i"; done

for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do  # C-style
    echo "$i"
done

while (( $# > 0 )); do           # process arguments with shift
    echo "$1"
    shift
done

count=10
until (( count < 0 )); do        # runs until the test succeeds
    echo "$count"
    (( count-- ))
done

while read -r line; do           # read a file line by line
    echo "$line"
done < "$file"

while IFS="," read -r num last first; do   # split each line on commas
    echo "$first $last"
done < students.txt
```

- `while` repeats while the test command succeeds (status 0); `until` repeats while it fails.
- `break` leaves the loop; `continue` skips to the next iteration.
- `for x in $str` (unquoted) loops over the words of `str`.
- Unquoted `$@` splits arguments that contain spaces: always write `"$@"`.

sections.title: 15. Arrays
sections.md:
| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `arr=(1 2 3)` | create (elements separated by spaces) |
| `arr=("a b" c)` | quote elements that contain spaces |
| `arr=("$@")` | array of the command line arguments |
| `arr[5]=x` | set element 5 (indexes may have gaps) |
| `${arr[i]}` | element *i* (braces required; `i` needs no `$`) |
| `$arr` | element 0 only (common mistake) |
| `${#arr[@]}` | number of elements |
| `"${arr[@]}"` | all elements, **one word each** (use this) |
| `"${arr[*]}"` | all elements as **one string** |
| `${!arr[@]}` | the list of indexes |
| `arr+=("$x")` | append one element |
| `a+=("${b[@]}")` | append all of `b` |
| `declare -a arr` | declare an (empty) array |
| `mapfile -t arr < f` | each line of `f` becomes an element |
| `read -a arr` | split one input line into an array |

```bash
n=${#arr[@]}
for (( i = 0; i < n; i++ )); do
    echo "$i: ${arr[i]}"
done

for elem in "${arr[@]}"; do echo "$elem"; done

tmp=${arr[i]}                  # swap elements i and j
arr[i]=${arr[j]}
arr[j]=$tmp

echo "${arr[@]}"               # print all on one line
```

sections.title: 16. Functions
sections.md:
```bash
max2() {                       # course style: name() { ... }
    if (( $1 >= $2 )); then
        echo "$1"              # "return" a value by printing it
    else
        echo "$2"
    fi
}
hi=$(max2 4 9)                 # capture it with command substitution

is_int() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^[-+]?[0-9]+$ ]]  # status of the last command is the function's status
}
if is_int "$x"; then echo "integer"; fi
```

- Called like a command: `max2 4 9` (no parentheses, no commas). Define a function **before** calling it.
- Inside, `$1 $2 ... $# "$@"` are the **function's** arguments; the script's arguments come back after it returns.
- `return n` ends the function with exit status *n* (0-255; 0 = success/true). Without `return` the status is that of the last command.
- **Dynamic scoping**: variables are global by default; a function can read and change the caller's variables (this is one way to hand back results, e.g. set `idx` and let the caller read it).
- `local x=5` makes `x` belong to the function (and functions it calls) so the caller's `x` is untouched. Always make loop counters local.
- Syntax: a space or newline after `{` and a newline (or `;`) before `}`.
- Sourcing a file of functions: `. ./lib.sh` (or `source ./lib.sh`).

```bash
# typical script layout for a long exam question
#!/bin/bash
helper() {
    local i
    ...
}
if (( $# == 0 )); then
    echo "Usage: prog.sh args..." >&2
    exit 1
fi
status=0
for arg in "$@"; do
    ...
done
exit "$status"
```
